verdicts.reason: The finding is refuted. The cell does not cite a text log. It says the messages are in "the sealed checkout", and the sealed checkout's git object store does hold those exact commit messages. `git cat-file -p` (read-only) on both objects in g05/cell/work prints "WIP on main: e8e9228 install Y" for 0a20e383 and "index on main: e8e9228 install Y" for 4e675634. Both object files are part of the sealed evidence: their sha256 values match the entries in g05/evidence.manifest.json. The rest of the finding is accurate but beside the point. bookkeeping.json records only IDs and paths, no text log contains the strings, and only Astra's note uses them. None of that makes the cell false, because the cell names a different sealed source, one the reviewer did not inspect. The round-1 verification of G5 made the same mistake: it said "no sealed g05 evidence contains the strings". The author then evidently checked the checkout's objects and cited them, so the round-1 rewrite is a correction, not an invented claim. The cell's short IDs `0a20e38` and `4e67563` match the full IDs. The proposed fix would delete true, sealed evidence, so it should not be applied. At most there is a small wording nit. "logged as" could be read as a reflog or `git log` entry, but the stash was popped, so the objects are unreachable and neither shows them. Replacing "logged as" with "whose commit messages read" would remove that ambiguity. No fact or decision changes either way.
